channel.title: Doctor's Notes by Dr. OMEB
channel.description: The business behind the noise: music, marketing, audience growth, and creative technology.

item.title: How TikTok Livestreaming Rewired My Marketing Brain
item.description: After twenty years of treating bars as the only real room, Dr. OMEB nearly quit. Then a weekly livestream became a virtual concert, a content engine, and Rock n' Roll Church.

item.title: Nobody Owes You Attention
item.description: A bad LinkedIn exchange revealed a useful marketing truth: attention cannot be invoiced, bartered, or demanded. It has to be earned.

item.title: What 1.2 Million Royalty Transactions Taught Me About Why Artists Need a Better Room
item.description: Dr. OMEB revisits his 2019 dissertation on 1.2 million royalty transactions, checks it against his own distributor history, and explains why artists need more than a streaming strategy.

item.title: I Spent $283 on TikTok Ads. Here's What the Experiment Taught Me.
item.description: A practical comparison of two Dr. OMEB TikTok Spark Ad campaigns: the results, the limits of the test, and what paid amplification can—and cannot—fix.

item.title: Your Brand Is Losing a War for Attention: KISS Figured Out How to Win It 50 Years Ago
item.description: KISS understood that a band competes with every available form of entertainment. Dr. OMEB translates that lesson into a practical brand framework.

item.title: AI Does Not Replace Taste: Why Creative Experience Matters More Now
item.description: AI can shorten the distance between an idea and an execution, but it does not supply taste, judgment, accountability, or a point of view.

item.title: How AI Let Me Make the Music Video I Could Never Afford
item.description: An honest look at the AI-assisted production of Dr. OMEB's Symptom of the Universe video featuring Vinny Appice: tools, failures, labor, and what the workflow really changed.
